messages:
ana: FYI, docs CI is failing on the latest PR — mkdocs-linkcheck flags a bunch of internal anchors as 404. I ran the build locally and see the same. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234 :eyes:

docsite-bot: CI job docs/build #142 failed — linkcheck returned exit code 2. Failing targets: /sdk/python#client-initialization, /guides/migrations#what-s-new, /api/ops#kv_cache

ana: (typo above, meant ana)

ana: Log excerpt:
```
Checking internal links...
  ✖  /guides/migrations#what-s-new -> 404 Not Found
  ✖  /sdk/python#client-initialization -> 404 Not Found
  ✖  /api/ops#kv_cache -> 404 Not Found
```

lee: Thanks — I saw this pattern before. Often it's a slug normalization mismatch between our MDX/Docusaurus and mkdocs-linkcheck. Docusaurus can slugify "What's new?" as "what-s-new" while mkdocs (or our plugin) might produce "whats-new" or vice-versa. Same for underscores vs dashes on anchors like kv_cache -> kv-cache.

sam: Can you paste the offending markdown/includes? Sometimes a fenced code block labeled `md` or `mdx` with a heading inside an include gets rendered differently by the site generator vs linkcheck.

ana: Here is the include from /guides/migrations.md (line ~12):
```md
<!-- include: examples/release-notes.md -->
```
And examples/release-notes.md starts with a header: `# What's new?` — that seems to be where the slug comes from.

lee: Yup. Also saw one where a code fence contained a heading (inside a triple-backtick block) and our preprocessor accidentally emitted the heading into the final HTML without matching the slug mkdocs generates. That produces a mismatch in the index vs anchor.

sam: Quick local check: run `mkdocs build --strict` + `mkdocs-linkcheck`. To normalize fast, you can map both variants in the nav to the same anchor. But cleaner is to pick one slugifier rule. A quick regex to find suspect anchors: 
```bash
rg "#(\w+_?\w+)" -n docs/ | sed -E 's/.*#//g' | sort -u
```
This shows underscores vs dashes.

jonathan: Pushed a tiny fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1237 — I replaced the `# What's new?` heading with an explicit anchor above the section and changed the internal links to point to `#whats-new` (the mkdocs slug). Diff attached. Also normalized kv_cache -> kv-cache in the API docs. Added a CI linkcheck preview step so PRs fail fast.

ana: Reproduced locally with jonathan's branch — linkcheck passes now. Thanks. Can someone review/merge? :pray:

lee: LGTM, left one nit about a blank line in the example include. Approving now. :thumbsup:

jonathan: Merged and pushed. Deploy job triggered.

docsite-bot: Deploy: docs/site deploy started for commit 8f3a1b2. Preview available at https://deploy-preview-1237--docs.redwood.ai

ana: Verified preview links — all internal anchors resolve. Nice catch. I'll update CONTRIBUTING.md with a short note: prefer explicit <a id=...> anchors for critical cross-page links and avoid headings with punctuation if you rely on automatic slugging.

sam: We should also add a small unit in the docs CI that compares Docusaurus vs mkdocs slug output for common headings so we catch differences automatically. Filing a follow-up ticket.

jonathan: filed ticket RED-457 in product backlog.

ana: Closing the thread — thanks everyone :tada:
